look_here_first: Start at the perennial basal rosette and nearly leafless flowering scapes. Because local T. scaposa can look very similar, confirm the taxonomic concept and provenance instead of identifying a scaped yellow daisy as acaulis by color.

project_inclusion.range_basis: B051 deep review: Kew/GRIN accept state-level Texas nativity, but reviewed var. acaulis is Panhandle/Great Plains-centered and no three qualifying target-zone counties were confirmed.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Do not count as confirmed target-zone native; scientific range FAIL is independent of learner admission.

best_field_traits: Leaves concentrated at the base; flowering stalks mostly leafless.
One yellow radiate head per scape.
Reviewed var. acaulis is Panhandle/Great Plains-centered; identity must not be inferred from a generic Central Texas four-nerve daisy.

comparisons.key_distinctions: T. linearifolia is an annual with leafy flowering stems. T. scaposa var. scaposa is the documented local perennial rosette-and-scape four-nerve daisy; T. acaulis overlaps morphologically, so use verified species/variety and geography rather than color alone.
